Substantial differences are observed between subgroups, indicating variability in the effects. Annex 3: Multiple Micronutrient Supplements (MMS) vs. Iron and Folic Acid Supplements (IFAS): 8. Outcomes assessed include anemia, cesarean section rates, maternal mortality, small-for-gestational-age births, low birth weight, preterm birth, congenital anomalies, perinatal mortality, and neonatal mortality. 9. A comparison was made between 4 mg folic acid supplementation and iron (30 mg or 60 mg) combined with folic acid supplementation. 10. The data source is a WHO-specified analysis based on findings from Keats EC, Haider BA, Tam E, Bhutta ZA, as published in the Cochrane Database of Systematic Reviews in 2019 (CD004905). 11. For some outcomes, no studies included data for subgroup analysis. 12. Wide confidence intervals crossing the line of no effect were observed in certain analyses, indicating imprecision. 13. Serious unexplained heterogeneity was noted in some comparisons, with an I² value of 60%. 14. Substantial subgroup differences were identified in certain analyses.
